units.sourceHTML: 7.7 Text search across multiple lines

units.text: This section uses ⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧ commands to search for consecutive words spanning multiple lines. See ⟦2⟧Multiline techniques - using D,G,H,N,P to process multiple lines⟦3⟧.
units.sourceHTML: This section uses N and D commands to search for consecutive words spanning multiple lines. See Multiline techniques - using D,G,H,N,P to process multiple lines.

units.text: These examples deal with finding doubled occurrences of words in a document.
units.sourceHTML: These examples deal with finding doubled occurrences of words in a document.

units.sourceHTML: When the doubled word span two lines the above regular expression will not find them as grep and sed operate line-by-line.

units.text: By using ⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧ commands, ⟦2⟧ can apply regular expressions on multiple lines (that is, multiple lines are stored in the pattern space, and the regular expression works on it):
units.sourceHTML: By using N and D commands, sed can apply regular expressions on multiple lines (that is, multiple lines are stored in the pattern space, and the regular expression works on it):

units.text: See the GNU ⟦0⟧ manual for an alternative solution using ⟦1⟧ and ⟦2⟧ at ⟦3⟧https://gnu.org/s/coreutils/manual/html_node/Squeezing-and-deleting.html⟦4⟧.
units.sourceHTML: See the GNU coreutils manual for an alternative solution using tr -s and uniq at https://gnu.org/s/coreutils/manual/html_node/Squeezing-and-deleting.html.

units.text: The regular expression ‘⟦0⟧’ searches for word-boundary (‘⟦1⟧’), followed by one-or-more word-characters (‘⟦2⟧’), followed by whitespace (‘⟦3⟧’). See ⟦4⟧regular expression extensions⟦5⟧.
units.sourceHTML: • The regular expression ‘\b\w+\s+’ searches for word-boundary (‘\b’), followed by one-or-more word-characters (‘\w+’), followed by whitespace (‘\s+’). See regular expression extensions.

units.text: Adding parentheses around the ‘⟦0⟧’ expression creates a subexpression. The regular expression pattern ‘⟦1⟧’ defines a subexpression (in the parentheses) followed by a back-reference, separated by whitespace. A successful match means the ⟦2⟧ was repeated twice in succession. See ⟦3⟧Back-references and Subexpressions⟦4⟧.
units.sourceHTML: • Adding parentheses around the ‘(\w+)’ expression creates a subexpression. The regular expression pattern ‘(PATTERN)\s+\1’ defines a subexpression (in the parentheses) followed by a back-reference, separated by whitespace. A successful match means the PATTERN was repeated twice in succession. See Back-references and Subexpressions.

units.text: The word-boundery expression (‘⟦0⟧’) at both ends ensures partial words are not matched (e.g. ‘⟦1⟧’ is not a desired match).
units.sourceHTML: • The word-boundery expression (‘\b’) at both ends ensures partial words are not matched (e.g. ‘the then’ is not a desired match).

units.text: The ⟦0⟧ option enables extended regular expression syntax, alleviating the need to add backslashes before the parenthesis. See ⟦1⟧Overview of extended regular expression syntax⟦2⟧.
units.sourceHTML: • The -E option enables extended regular expression syntax, alleviating the need to add backslashes before the parenthesis. See Overview of extended regular expression syntax.

units.text: The ⟦0⟧ command appends the next line to the pattern space (thus ensuring it contains two consecutive lines in every cycle).
units.sourceHTML: • The N command appends the next line to the pattern space (thus ensuring it contains two consecutive lines in every cycle).

units.text: The regular expression uses ‘⟦0⟧’ for word separator which matches both spaces and newlines.
units.sourceHTML: • The regular expression uses ‘\s+’ for word separator which matches both spaces and newlines.

units.text: The regular expression matches, the entire pattern space is printed with ⟦0⟧. No lines are printed by default due to the ⟦1⟧ option.
units.sourceHTML: • The regular expression matches, the entire pattern space is printed with p. No lines are printed by default due to the -n option.

units.text: The ⟦0⟧ removes the first line from the pattern space (up until the first newline), readying it for the next cycle.
units.sourceHTML: • The D removes the first line from the pattern space (up until the first newline), readying it for the next cycle.
